subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this permanent global operational-notice contract, including fail-closed source suppression when a configured operator-session redirect cannot be written?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent and proof-positive, but choosing confidentiality over notice availability on redirect failure—and exposing that choice through config, durable session state, and Plugin SDK—is a product and security-boundary decision that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the privacy-first contract
options.body: Accept all four modes, keep redirect failures source-silent with operator-visible logging, and refresh and re-review the exact head before merge.

options.title: Require durable redirect recovery
options.body: Delay redirect mode until failed operator-session writes can be retained for operator-only retry without exposing notices to the source chat.

options.title: Narrow to non-redirect modes
options.body: Land always, once, and silent while deferring redirect and its privacy-versus-availability contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the privacy-first contract
recommendation.body: Accept all four modes, keep redirect failures source-silent with operator-visible logging, and refresh and re-review the exact head before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: His history spans the visible-reply, suppression, session, heartbeat, plugin-hook, and config boundaries needed to accept this cross-cutting contract.
